title: What are the other angles when the smallest is sixty?
description: A figure has sixty degrees as its smallest angle of symmetry. The smallest angle is added again and again until the full turn is reached. The list is checked by counting the turns that make the full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: the other angles of symmetry are the multiples of the smallest angle, up to the full turn. Watch for students who stop before the full turn or leave it out.

source: Figure it Out Q4 (section 9.2, second block)
video_script.why: The child lists all the angles of symmetry of a figure whose smallest angle is sixty degrees.
video_script.substitution: a figure turned about its dot, with the smallest angle added again and again, the way the book builds its lists
video_script.anchor: a figure with a dot at its centre, turned by sixty degrees each time
video_script.payoff_line: The other angles are the next five multiples of sixty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the other angles are one hundred twenty, one hundred eighty, two hundred forty, three hundred and three hundred sixty degrees

maths_rules: the angles of symmetry are the multiples of the smallest angle, up to 360°
check: 360 ÷ 60 = 6, so there are 6 angles of symmetry in all: 60° and the five others
video_script.design: A figure turned by sixty degrees again and again, with each total written under the last. The list ends at the full turn, and the count of six turns is the check.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, about a figure.
<bookmark mark='fig'/>Its smallest angle of symmetry is sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are its other angles of symmetry?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the windmill with ticks at 90°, 180°, 270°, 360°; each is a multiple of 90°

marks.mill: the windmill turns and ticks appear at 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°

narration: <bookmark mark='mill'/>The windmill in your book fits after four turns.
They are ninety, one hundred eighty, two hundred seventy and three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Each one is the smallest angle, taken again and again.

beats.on_screen: Given: the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure is 60°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure is sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the other angles of symmetry
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the other angles of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: every angle of symmetry is a multiple of the smallest: 60° x 1, 60° x 2, 60° x 3, ... up to 360°

marks.rule: the rule every angle is a multiple of 60° is written
marks.up: the words up to 360° are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, every angle of symmetry is a multiple of the smallest angle.
<bookmark mark='up'/>We go on until we reach the full turn.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, two times sixty is one hundred twenty, and three times sixty is one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four times sixty is two hundred forty, and five times sixty is three hundred.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six times sixty is three hundred sixty, the full turn.

beats.on_screen: check: 6 x 60° = 360°, the full turn; 360 ÷ 60 = 6, so there are 6 angles in all: 60° and 5 others

marks.count: 360 ÷ 60 = 6 is written, and the six angles are counted

narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Step three, check the list.
Six turns of sixty degrees make three hundred sixty, the full turn.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Three hundred sixty divided by sixty is six, so there are six angles in all.
Sixty is the first, and five others follow it.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The other angles are the next five multiples of sixty degrees.
They are one hundred twenty, one hundred eighty, two hundred forty, three hundred and three hundred sixty.
